newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Ex-Colombian leader treated for bleeding ulcer.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Colombian leader treated for bleeding ulcer.

text.p: Former Colombian president Virgilio Barco, who presided over the most violent chapter of his country's war with powerful drug lords, underwent surgery on Wednesday for treatment of a bleeding ulcer.
A statement from the Fundacion Santa Fe hospital in Bogota said Barco, who turned 75 earlier this month, was in stable condition with no immediate sign of any complications.

A report on the RCN radio network said Barco, a shy technocrat long known for being ill at ease with the press, had been diagnosed with stomach cancer. But a hospital spokesmen declined to comment on the report, citing a family request for confidentiality.

Barco -- a former government minister and mayor of Bogota who holds a doctorate in economic science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology -- emerged from relative political obscurity in May 1986 to win the biggest landslide ever recorded in a Colombian presidential race.
Wielding what he called at the time "an unequivocal mandate for change," he vowed to fight poverty and rid Colombia of the violence that has ravaged it for decades.

The country's security situation deteriorated steadily during his four-year term, however, as drug lords led by Pablo Escobar, the late chieftain of the Medellin cartel, launched a nationwide campaign of terror featuring assassinations and bombings aimed at scuttling a U.S.-Colombian extradition treaty.

Colombia's Congress clamped a constitutional ban on extradition in 1991, a year after Barco handed over power to Cesar Gaviria, a fellow member of the country's Liberal Party who now serves as secretary-general of the Organisation of American States.
Barco, who reportedly suffers from Alzheimer's disease, rarely appears in public. He is one of six living ex-presidents in Colombia.
